By selling an article, Michael earned a profit equal to one-fourth of the price he bought it. If he sold it for ₹ 375, what was the cost price?
explanation: Let C.P. = x. Profit = x/4. S.P. = x + x/4 = 5x/4 = 375. So x = 300.

text: If the cost price of 15 books is equal to the selling price of 20 books, the loss percent is
explanation: CP of 15 = SP of 20. Let CP of each = 1. SP of 20 books = 15. SP of each = 15/20 = 3/4. Loss = 1/4. Loss% = 25%.

text: By selling 33 metres of cloth, one gains the selling price of 11 metres. Find the gain percent.
explanation: SP of 33 − CP of 33 = SP of 11. So CP of 33 = SP of 22. SP/CP = 33/22 = 3/2. Gain% = (1/2) × 100 = 50%.

explanation: CP of 17 − 720 = CP of 5. CP of 12 = 720. CP of 1 ball = 720/12 = ₹ 60.

text: A vendor loses the selling price of 4 oranges on selling 36 oranges. His loss percent is
explanation: Loss = SP of 4. CP of 36 = SP of 36 + SP of 4 = SP of 40. Loss% = (4/40) × 100 = 10%.

A man sells a book at a profit of 20%. If he had bought it at 20% less and sold it for ₹ 18 less, he would have gained 25%. The cost price of the book is
explanation: Let CP = x. SP = 1.2x. New CP = 0.8x. New SP = 1.2x − 18. For 25% gain: 1.2x − 18 = 0.8x × 1.25 = x. So 0.2x = 18. x = 90.

If selling price is doubled, the profit triples. Find the profit percent.
explanation: Let CP = C, SP = S. Profit P = S − C. If SP doubles: 2S − C = 3P = 3(S − C). 2S − C = 3S − 3C. 2C = S. Profit% = (S − C)/C × 100 = C/C × 100 = 100%.

text: A man sold two flats at the rate of ₹ 1.995 lakhs each. On one he gains 5% and on the other, he loses 5%. His gain or loss percent in the whole transaction is
explanation: When two items are sold at same price with equal gain% and loss%, there is always a loss. Loss% = (5)²/100 = 0.25%.

explanation: CP of 1 orange = 10/5 = ₹ 2. SP of 1 orange = 15/6 = ₹ 2.50. Profit = 0.50. Profit% = (0.50/2) × 100 = 25%.
